items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: my dad would take me to hear guys that would come into town, like Oscar Peterson and Buddy DeFranco and Dizzy Gillespie

ctx.x: Do you recall when you started figuring out the mystery of chord symbols and how they might apply to your improvising?

Yeah I do. When we got together to play it was just sort of a free for all you know. And I finally figured out oh, yeah, they’re playing the form and there’s a thing called a bridge you know. And you just don’t stop playing until you wear out and stop. You actually follow this form. So yeah, that dawned on me and I started listening to music more intently and talking to my friends. And also at that time my dad would take me to hear guys that would come into town, like Oscar Peterson and Buddy DeFranco and Dizzy…

I wonder if you ever had a private teacher that said to you — this would have been your classical teacher — that said, “Listen you have to choose. I can hear this jazz thing going on in your sound on this Mozart and this won’t do at all.” Did that ever happen to you?
